newsitem.title: CANADA: CIBC chairman says rates close to bottom.
newsitem.headline: CIBC chairman says rates close to bottom.

text.p: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce chairman Al Flood said on Monday that Canadian interest rates are getting close to bottoming out.

The Bank of Canada earlier today cut its key bank rate to 3.50 percent from 3.75 percent, the lowest short-term interest rates in Canada in 33 years. Canada's major chartered banks quickly lowered their prime lending rates to 5 percent from 5.25 percent, their lowest level since July 1956.
"These are very good rates. I think we're getting near the bottom. I would suggest we might see some further movement, but very little," Flood told reporters after a speech.
The latest rate reduction was the 10th this year and the 19th since Canada's central bank began cutting in May 1995 to spur a sluggish Canadian economy.

Flood said his bank saw signs that the rate cuts were having an effect. "It's certainly been in the last 90 days that we've really seen low real interest rates when you look at inflation. I think we should let this happen and I think over the medium term we'll see some improvement," Flood said. Last week, CT Financial Services boosted its loan loss provision and suggested others may follow. But Flood said CIBC's losses were not threatening to exceed its provisions.

"We've been fairly conservative with our loan loss provision all the way through and we'll continue that policy. We haven't seen losses running in excess of our provisioning at this stage," Flood said.
CT Financial increased its credit loss provision to C$29 million in the third quarter from C$22 million in the second quarter.
CT Financial said it believed the industry would see higher personal loan arrears due to flat personal incomes, high consumer debt and low savings rates.
